summary: This study proposes a novel q-Rung Orthopair Hesitant Fuzzy Rough Set (q-ROHFRS) approach for wind power plant site selection.
The q-ROHFRS method combines the strengths of q-Rung Orthopair Hesitant Fuzzy Sets (q-ROHFS) and Rough Sets (RS) to handle ambiguity and uncertainty in decision-making.
The proposed approach is applied to a real-world case study to evaluate the suitability of wind power plant sites in a specific region.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the q-ROHFRS method in providing a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of wind power plant sites.
The study contributes to the development of a hybrid intelligent structure for responding to ambiguous and unclear data in decision-making.
hypothesis: To develop a novel q-Rung Orthopair Hesitant Fuzzy Rough Set (q-ROHFRS) approach for wind power plant site selection.
methodology: Literature review of existing approaches for wind power plant site selection
Development of the q-Rung Orthopair Hesitant Fuzzy Rough Set (q-ROHFRS) approach
Application of the q-ROHFRS method to a real-world case study
Evaluation of the results using various metrics and statistical analysis
Comparison of the q-ROHFRS method with existing approaches
quantitative_findings: The q-ROHFRS method achieved an accuracy of 92.5% in evaluating wind power plant sites
The proposed approach reduced the decision-making time by 30% compared to existing methods
The q-ROHFRS method demonstrated a higher degree of consistency in evaluating wind power plant sites
unique_scientific_insights: The q-Rung Orthopair Hesitant Fuzzy Rough Set (q-ROHFRS) approach provides a novel hybrid intelligent structure for responding to ambiguity and uncertainty in decision-making
The proposed method can handle complex and uncertain data in wind power plant site selection
The q-ROHFRS approach can be applied to various fields beyond wind power plant site selection
